questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personal interest in Japan and its culture. I wanted to combine the academic life of a student with exploring its culture, building bridges between the two.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In short, I'd recommend anyone with the courage and interest to use the opportunity to study abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Japan is very bureaucratic and very analog with a lot of paperwork compared to Denmark. Thus, systems were in place for almost everything even though clear information in English were often lacking. Communication with other students and dorm mates helped out a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assisted by especially the management of my dorm for translation and instructions of needed registration, insurance, pension at the city hall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The host institution were always helpful in assisting, although I mainly got assisted by my dormitory's management (affiliated to the university) out of the convenience of them being close by.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Although off-campus, I lived in a dormitory owned by the university. Applying to said dormitory was an option given in the general application process to the university and was, in my opinion, the easier way to find accomodation compared to having find other options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That transportion is required to campus, and most likely multiple campuses depending on choice of courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Global Village Tsukumodai was, probably, the best place for me to live due to big community of other international students living there. It made it easier to find friends and memories, share the same courses, register at the city hall together and so on. Although a bit pricy (for me a little over  3000DKK, 60K yen) it was all worth it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of information was giving, but getting used to the student portal and how to access information online was a little tedious.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the registration process a little hard but doable with the help of others who had to register as well. I feel like we were given a lot of information, but everything you needed for registration was there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was but helped by flat mates, the management of my dormitory and by mail by my host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Having prior course approval (forhåndsgodkendelse) made getting an overview of possible courses for me to take a lot easier. I picked from my list, trying to make a realistic schedule where the courses lined up and where days were at the same campus. I found it easy to register with the information I was given.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to, not only pick courses that you have preapproval for, but make sure the schedule that you're putting together is realistic so you don't have to commute from different campuses on the same day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic program was at a lower level than my home university, but had some interesting topics that were refreshing to explore.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Although a master student, I was given permission take also take BA-courses since the length of a bachelor in Japan is 4 years. Academic level of BA-courses varied a lot and were noticably lower level than the MA-courses I took.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lectures and less discussion. I recommend seminar courses for more in-class discussion that I believe we are more used to in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sociological Theory, Introduction to International Understanding, Multicultural Coexistance, Social Innovation and Social Design, Approaches to Understanding Cultures, Japanese JA200.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I especially enjoyed learning Japanese in a "real" Japanese language class. Probably not for everyone, but if you have the interest and motivation I highly recommend it.

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Apart from travel insurance from home, international students in Japan are required to pay obligatory insurance and pension monthly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Investing in a second hand bike for transportation to campus is ideal to save money on especially the monorail. Bike can be resold upon returning to Dennmark. Food is affordable if you decided to cook a lot on your own - with the exception of fruit and some vegetables. Eating out is cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed most of my social life with my flat mates. I tried joining one Social Circle, a volleyball sports club, but I was the only Westerner and no one spoke english, making it very hard to fit in and adjust.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many social events were hold by my dormitory, often introducing Japanese culture and seasonal events. It was easy to apply and a convenient way of meeting people from other units within the dorm.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depening on the budget, I would recommend travelling around Japan as much as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travelling, eating out, exploring the city in which you life.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: On the same time, easy and difficult. Japanese people speak very little English, often making it hard to communicate. Easy as Japanese culture is organized and convenient, e.g. transportation with no delays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask question if you are uncertain about anything. Other students is in the exact same position as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most aspects, but especially food culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to make a rough budget for your coming stay. Get your main expenses down to get a rough idea of how much you can/want to travel.
2. Prepare as much as possible in terms of orientating and getting yourself familiar with course list, the credit transfer to ECTS. and so on.
3. ASK QUESTIONS, everyone is ready to help you in Japan, both host institution, dorm mates and random stranges if you get lost or need help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to get an overview and apply for scholarships and funds. Many people are too lazy to do this, but applying to a lot will most likely result in you getting some kind of financial support for your stay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To explore and to immerse into another culture with likeminded peers/students. An unforgettable experience and a unique opportunity to live in another country if that is on your bucket list.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To adjust to the culture and bureaucracy of Japan, having to do everything in person when registering as a foreigner/student.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
